working_title: Scotland's Kintyre and Islay Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing the Far West
angle: Kintyre and neighbouring Islay together form one of the most rewarding and underplayed links circuits in Britain, anchored by Machrihanish, Machrihanish Dunes and Dunaverty on the peninsula and The Machrie on Islay. The post makes the logistical case for treating both destinations as a single trip rather than separate pilgrimages, with honest advice on the effort involved in getting there.
research_notes:
- Kintyre Peninsula: a narrow 40-mile stretch of land on Scotland's west coast, served by the A83 from Glasgow or by CalMac ferry from Ardrossan to Campbeltown (avoids the long road loop around Argyll). Drive from Glasgow is roughly four hours; ferry option cuts the road distance significantly.
- Machrihanish Golf Club: founded 1876 as Kintyre Golf Club; Old Tom Morris redesigned and expanded to 18 holes in 1879, including the famous opening drive across the Atlantic beach. Widely regarded as one of the great natural links in the British Isles.
- Machrihanish Dunes: opened 2009, designed by David McLay Kidd (who grew up on Kintyre). Notably the only course in the world built and laid out on a Site of Specific Scientific Interest (SSSI). Has developed into a full resort with on-site accommodation.
- Dunaverty Golf Club: 18-hole par-66 natural links roughly 15 minutes south of Machrihanish in the village of Southend. Overlooks Sanda Island, Ailsa Craig, Ayrshire coast and (on clear days) Northern Ireland to the southwest. Described as a good mix of holes suitable for low and high handicappers.
- Kintyre packs three links courses (Machrihanish, Machrihanish Dunes, Dunaverty) within easy driving distance of each other, making a two- or three-night stay feasible for playing all three.
- Islay add-on: CalMac ferry from Kennacraig (on the Kintyre peninsula, just south of Tarbert) to Port Ellen or Port Askaig; crossing approx 2 hours 10 minutes to Port Ellen. Alternatively, Loganair flies from Glasgow to Islay in roughly 45 minutes.
- The Machrie, Islay: original Willie Campbell design dating to 1891; fully redesigned in 2018 by David J. Russell to modern championship standard. Stretches over 7,000 yards from the back tees. Ranked in Golf Monthly's Top 100 UK and Ireland courses. Resort (Another Place, The Machrie) also offers hotel accommodation, a six-hole 'Wee Course', putting course ('The Hebrides'), short-game area and Trackman simulator. Resort is closed for a winter period (historically mid-November to mid-February — confirm dates before booking).
- The Machrie famously hosted a 1901 match between Vardon, Braid and Taylor, reportedly for the largest prize of its kind in the British Isles at that time.
- Gulf Stream runs along the west coast of Kintyre, giving a marginally milder climate than much of Scotland.
- Practical note: CalMac car ferry bookings for Islay should be made well in advance, especially in summer. Pedestrians can buy tickets on the day but car spaces fill up.
- Glencruitten (Oban Golf Club) is home course of Robert MacIntyre — worth a mention as a mainland Argyll detour context point, though not central to this Kintyre/Islay circuit.
- The Machrie also links naturally to distillery tourism on Islay (Laphroaig, Lagavulin, Ardbeg nearby) — useful non-golf context for travelling companions or rest days.
